CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFHTMLHEAD

CFHTMLHEAD lets code anywhere in a page (a custom tag, an included file, the bottom of a long template) add a <META>, <STYLE>, <SCRIPT> or <TITLE> to the document head after the head has already been written.

Category

Output and page processing

Syntax

<CFHTMLHEAD TEXT="text">

Attributes

TEXT
Required. The text to add. Double any quotation marks that match the ones around the value.

Usage

The text is inserted when the page is finished, just before the first </HEAD> tag of the output. If the page has no </HEAD>, it goes at the very top. Several CFHTMLHEAD tags add their text in order.

It is particularly useful in custom tags that need JavaScript functions or styles defined once in the head of the calling page. Text is ignored if the page is replaced with CFCONTENT FILE.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<HTML>
<HEAD><TITLE>CFHTMLHEAD example</TITLE></HEAD>
<BODY>
<H3 CLASS="fancy">A heading styled from the bottom of the page</H3>
<P>The style sheet for the heading above is defined by a CFHTMLHEAD tag that runs
after the heading has been written. View the source of this frame to see where it went.</P>
<CFSET Shade = "##336699">
<CFHTMLHEAD TEXT="<STYLE TYPE=""text/css"">H3.fancy { color: #Shade#; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; }</STYLE>">
</BODY>
</HTML>

See also

CFHEADER, CFCONTENT, CFMODULE
